title: Production Change Management Standard (v1)
author: Aisha Rahman
content:
h1. Purpose
This standard sets out what Redwood Inference treats as a production change and the minimum steps to plan, approve, execute and validate one. It aims to limit customer impact without slowing engineering down.

h1. Scope
Covers every production environment for the Hosted API and Console:
* Hosted API control plane and data plane services
* Console UI and backend
* Shared platform dependencies (routing, auth, billing metering, observability agents)

Not covered: customer-managed *Private deployment* environments (see the Private Deployment Change Policy) and vendor-managed maintenance outside Redwood's control.

h1. Definitions
* *Production:* any environment serving external customer traffic, including canary and regional production.
* *Production change:* anything that can affect confidentiality, integrity, availability, latency, cost or correctness of customer-facing workloads.
* *Change owner:* the person accountable for the change from start to finish.
* *Approver:* the peer, manager, SRE or security reviewer required for the risk tier.
* *Change record:* the ticket plus links documenting intent, risk, approvals, execution and validation.

h1. Change types
|| Change type || When used || Required approvals || Notes ||
| Standard | Low risk, pre-approved pattern (doc-only, internal dashboard fixes, non-prod config) | 1 peer approval | Must follow an approved standard template |
| Normal | Most production code/config deploys | 1 peer approval + (1) service owner approval | Pre-deploy verification, canary and comms assessment required |
| Emergency | Mitigating an active incident or preventing imminent customer impact | On-call incident commander (IC) + service owner approval (as available) | Retrospective change record required within 72 hours |

h1. What counts as a production change (non-exhaustive)
* Deployments to production clusters, canary regions included
* Routing, fallback or model selection policy changes
* Auth, RBAC, API key, rate limit, quota or billing meter changes
* Schema migrations, backfills or data retention configuration changes
* Infrastructure changes affecting capacity, autoscaling or failover
* Observability pipeline changes that could reduce visibility

h1. Minimum required artifacts
Every production change needs a change record containing:
* What is changing and the expected customer impact
* A rollback plan (stated explicitly, even if it is "redeploy the previous build")
* A verification plan
* Links to PR(s), build(s), dashboards, the runbook used and any migration plan
* Recorded approvals

h1. Risk assessment checklist
Answer before asking for approval:
1. Does it touch auth, data paths, encryption, logging or retention?
2. Does it alter request routing, batching, caching or model version selection?
3. Could it materially change token accounting or billing?
4. Does it involve a data migration or backfill?
5. Can it be rolled back quickly and safely (< 10 minutes), restoring the customer experience?

Any "yes" to 1–4 makes the change at least *Normal*, and it may need Security Review under the Secure SDLC requirements.

h1. Approvals
* *Peer approval:* an engineer in the same org who knows the subsystem.
* *Service owner approval:* the tech lead or on-call owner of the service.
* *SRE gate:* for changes to capacity, SLO-sensitive paths, traffic routing or failover config.
* *Security gate:* for changes to auth, secrets, encryption, audit logging, PII or data retention.

h1. Change windows and freezes
* Default window: weekdays 10:00–15:00 local time for the primary owning team.
* No changes during declared change freezes.
* Extra restrictions apply when error budgets are low (see "Change Freeze and Risk Assessment").

h1. Execution requirements
Every production change must:
1. Follow the documented runbook for the target system (Hosted API or Console).
2. Roll out via canary for traffic-bearing services unless the change record documents an exemption.
3. Check observability before and after (golden signals and the relevant dashboards).
4. Define a rollback trigger up front and apply "stop the line" when it fires.

h1. Communications requirements
The change owner decides whether customers need to be told:
* *Planned maintenance:* status page notice plus direct customer comms when material impact is expected.
* *No expected customer impact:* post in #deploys and make sure on-call knows if it is during core hours.
Templates and lead times are in "Planned Maintenance and Change Communications".

h1. Post-change validation and closure
Within 30 minutes after completion, the change owner must:
* Check key SLO metrics and error rates are normal
* Confirm the canary was healthy before full rollout
* Record results in the change record with screenshots/links
* Open follow-ups for any issues found

h1. References
* Prod Deployment Gates (Hosted API + Console)
* Hosted API Deploy Runbook
* Console Deploy Runbook
